about: What a browser sees when an address it opened fails (src/browser-pages.mjs, reached through parts/ui/show/server-rendered-page/page-egress.mjs). Rows are read in order and the first whose `when` matches is used: `host` matches the address's host (the live host's calm rows: how the workspace looks, `picture`, at full width, never a broken page), `path_starts` matches the start of the address, `status` the answer's status, and a row with no `when` matches everything. `route_words: true` shows what the route itself said (a plain line such as 'This link has expired') in place of `body`, unless it is one of `quiet_words`, which add nothing to the heading. An action's `href` is an address, or `{ "from": "request", "key": "path" }` for the address that failed. `quote: true` adds one line of Trillion's own voice from src/error-page-lines.json. `illustration` is `{ src, alt }`, the drawing above the words (assets/illustrations/, served under /workspace/illustrations/). `emphasis` is the look word every such page's words are drawn in (the shared page shell's centred card). An action's `again_seconds` presses it by itself after that many seconds (twice at most for one address), saying its `pending` words meanwhile. `ask_ai: true` adds the person's own AI as the way forward: their chosen AI (remembered from the workspace in the trillion_choice_ai cookie, src/ask-your-ai.mjs) as a button, and every AI app that opens a chat from an address as a logo chip under the actions, after `ask.choose` (no AI chosen yet) or `ask.others`, each opening a new chat in a new tab with `ask.prompt` ({heading} what failed, {page} the address, {said} what the route said).

ask.prompt: Something in Trillion did not work and I want your help. What failed: {heading}. Where: {page}. What Trillion answered: {said}. Use your Trillion connection to check what happened and fix it or do it another way. If you are not connected to Trillion yet, help me connect first.
